title: In-process scheduler
lead: One background thread runs registered interval jobs one at a time, and only one process per data directory runs them.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** any job (recipe pull is S11, IMAP polling S32, pings S42); time-of-day schedules (S42 decides how it picks the minute); a separate scheduler process or compose service; starting the thread under a WSGI server (S28 does that).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: S11, S32 and S42 each need a periodic task, and S28 was to choose the mechanism at the end of the MVP chain. A small stdlib scheduler keeps ADR 0002 (stdlib first) and the single container (NF7). The lock file stops duplicate jobs when a WSGI server starts several processes.

sections.heading: Owner input
sections.body:
Confirm (recommended as written): one daemon thread; jobs run one at a time in registration order; an exclusive lock file `$LARDER_DATA/scheduler.lock` (`fcntl.flock`, POSIX only) so a second process on the same data directory runs no jobs; the dev server starts it, `create_app` and the tests do not.

Owner decisions: approved as written, 2026-11-03. Spec-check note: the first run of a job is registration time plus one interval; state that in the tests.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/larder/scheduler.py`
- `src/larder/web/__init__.py` (`create_app` builds the scheduler and stores it in `app.extensions["larder.scheduler"]`; it does not start it)
- `src/larder/__main__.py` (start it before `app.run`, stop it afterwards)
- `tests/test_scheduler.py`

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
In `tests/test_scheduler.py` (an injected clock; no sleeping except the thread tests):
1. `test_job_runs_when_its_interval_has_elapsed_and_not_before`
2. `test_due_jobs_run_one_at_a_time_in_registration_order`
3. `test_next_run_is_one_interval_after_the_job_finishes`
4. `test_failing_job_is_logged_and_does_not_stop_the_others` (`assertLogs("larder.scheduler")`)
5. `test_register_rejects_duplicate_names_and_non_positive_intervals`
6. `test_start_runs_jobs_on_a_thread_and_stop_joins_it` (an `Event` with a timeout, interval 0.01 s)
7. `test_second_scheduler_on_the_same_data_dir_runs_no_jobs`
8. `test_stop_releases_the_lock_so_another_scheduler_can_run`
9. `test_create_app_does_not_start_the_thread` (in `tests/test_web_shell.py::AppFactoryTest`)
10. `test_main_starts_the_scheduler_before_the_dev_server` (in `MainTest`; patch `flask.Flask.run`)

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. `Scheduler(data_dir, clock=time.monotonic)` with `register(name, interval_seconds, func)`, `run_due()`, `start()`, `stop()` and a `running` property. A job is a no-argument callable; callers close over their settings.
2. `run_due()` runs each due job inside `try/except Exception`, logs a failure with `logging.getLogger("larder.scheduler")`, and schedules the next run one interval after the job finishes.
3. `start()` takes the lock with `flock(LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB)`; if it cannot, it logs once and returns without a thread. Otherwise it starts a daemon thread that loops: `run_due()`, then waits on a stop `Event` for at most one second.
4. `stop()` sets the event, joins the thread and releases the lock. `start()` twice is a no-op.
5. Wire it into `create_app` and `main` as listed in Files.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- Scheduler tests and the full suite pass; `ruff check .` is clean.
- The dev server starts and stops without hanging or leaving a thread.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Commit only when the owner asks; no AI attribution.
